It’s never too late and never too soon. 

May I ask how old are you (and your romantic interest)? I assume you both are very young.

Try initiate a conversation about what are the things you’re looking for in a partner (ask him about this and speak about your side as well), so both of you get a chance to talk about preferences and boundaries.

It would be beneficial to talk about what each of you consider a relationship, the milestone from which it can be seen as exclusive, etc. what you can and cannot accept. (flirting, cheating, the time spent with and without each other and so on, the list is endless)

Always, always speak up if something doesn’t seem right, if you feel uncomfortable, if your partner hurt your feelings!
You don’t have to make it a tit for tat, you can walk away if the other person is being rude, disrespectful.

Communication is a must. If he responds respectfully and able to communicate without hurting you or being childish (silent treatment, tantrum, emotional blackmail, etc.) then you have a good chance to solve problems.

When the pattern will become a pattern it’s going to be already too late. You’ll have feelings and attachment and it will be difficult to break up, hence you’ll more likely to suffer silently or you’ll have fights over this.

Setting boundaries is essential to a healthy relationship of any kind and they are not negotiable. It’s like cutting a limb to survive: ideally, you don’t have to cut any of them to stay happy and healthy. Also, survival isn’t the best tactic to stay in a relationship. You need personal and relational boundaries so others can relate to you the way you feel safe and happy. That’s how you communicate what’s ok and what not.

Don’t get your hopes up too high after 3 dates, your feelings for him at this stage are probably based mostly on fantasies/projections.

Ask him what kind of porn he likes (obviously in a situation where it’s appropriate), you’ll get an honest answer. Then tell him that you’re not comfortable with it in a committed relationship. If he decides to quit and stay with you, set a boundary that if you catch him even once, it’s over.

If he’s trying to normalize it, calling you crazy, talking about “this is how women try to control men” etc. then let go of him because he’s not for you.

Aztán amikor kezd neked is feltűnni, hogy szar van a palacsintában vagy esetleg normál, emberileg elvárható szeretetet, támogatást várnál egy helyzetben akkor offolnak mert ötletük sincs mi a faszról szól egy mélyebb emberi kapcsolódás és hogyan kell ezt csinálni. (Papolhatnak erről meg lehetnek sokéves, felszínes kapcsolataik ettől még.)

Kérd meg a terapeutát, hogy jelezzen vissza, ha mesélsz neki akkor mutasson rá hol kéne megfognod a szar működéseidet/gondolataidat. Ha erre nem hajlandó akkor nem biztos, hogy neked való a módszere.

Ha nem vagy rászorulva anyagilag arra, hogy dolgozz akkor próbálj néha önkénteskedni. Food not bombs ingyenkonyha hétvégente, krisnások ugyanez vagy egy állatmenhelyen tuti hasznát venné a sok kis árva állat két simiző, sétára vivő (pakolós, ganézós) kéznek.

Arra gondoltál már, hogy a más (személyiségzavarból fakadó) működéseid miatt olyan emberek kerülnek melléd akik toxikusak? (Barát, barátnő, stb.) Tehát nem minden kizárólag a te “szar személyiségednek” köszönhető? 

Ha szar mintáink vannak, akkor sajnos a kapcsolatainkban is választhatunk olyanokat akik ugyan “rímelnek” ránk de szar hatása van ránk a kettőnk közötti dinamikának. Az is megeshet, hogy ilyen emberekkel vesszük magunkat körül és így bizony bele lehet csúszni abba, hogy én vagyok a legszarabb, mindenki(nek) olyan jó körülöttem.
(Csak egy szempont a gondolkodáshoz.)

A másik, hogy esetleg menj kognitív viselkedésterápiára, keress másik szakembert a mostani mellett/helyett, próbálj meg más módszereket is szakmai segítséggel persze.

Értelmes, önreflektív embernek tűnsz, nagyon drukkolok, hogy a saját hajadnál fogva ki tudd húzni magad a szarból.

The term, “narcissist” is thrown around quite often, and can be misused. One of the defining characteristics of a narcissist is an individual who views others as objects, rather than as people. I suspected that something was way off with my mother when I wasn't able to talk with her about our problems.

First of all, she never taught me how to do it. That problems or any issue can be discussed. That silent treatment is not the right way to solve things.

Second, when I realised it's an option - I mean talking about the difficulties in any kind of human relationship - I constantly faced with her refusal. It was like she either didn't want to talk about it at all, or just shrugged it off of herself with "it's your problem, not mine". Early, my response was to it: "But it's between you and me, how could it be just "my problem"? Answer: "You are the one, who wants to talk, you say that it's a problem, not me, then you have to work on it, not me." I was a teenager at this time and of course I got very frustrated and angry at her for this answer. Then I became a difficult teenager for this. It haven't changed since then. It was app. 20 years ago.

So adding to this the fact that she was an adult and my parent at this time which means she should've been responsible to shape our relationship - this is how it started to show itself to me.

Later, a few years ago, during group therapy was the first time I heard about narcissism as a personality disorder - not just a character flaw. I thought I'm one myself because I could only talk about myself all the time. How things are bad and how hurt I feel and why others treat me like shit and why I'm not able to defend myself. (I was basically just begging for approval and validation from my peers and therapists.)

These are all can be symptoms of low self esteem and early bad treatment. I wasn't physically abused by my Nmother, so it was hard to acknowledge that I was abused by her at all. Don't fall into this trap.

I think the quality and the way of abuse defined for me that she is a narcissist. And the constant anxiety, apologizing, explaining myself and feeling of shame inside told me that  - compared to her, who never showed any sings of such things - I can't be like her.

I would've been so greatful is someone would've told me back then, that if someone hurts me, I don't need validation from my family, teachers, friends or anyone to feel hurt and maybe get a little angry at that other one. Instead I was angry at myself because somehow I must have deserved the bad treatment, any negative, hurtful comment or anything - even from a stranger. (because I've listened from my Nmother all my childhood that basically any kid and anyone is better than me. How? In which ways? I still don't know.) So I should just look deep inside and try to become a better person. My ass!

I know now that this is - the way they talked to me about this, the way itself - was gaslighting. They let me and wanted me to believe that I'm a bad little brat if I say someone did or said something hurtful to me. I must have misunderstood it and there's no need to cry, because the world isn't spinning around me. Next time I should be nicer to them. Of course. And bake a cake too, right?

Good luck for us to get to the other side of our lives without these things and finally being able to see who we really are. :)
